memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Whoever sits on anything that the man with a discharge sat on must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening. Whoever touches the man who has a discharge must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and they will be unclean till evening.'" - Lev 15:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the detail that must have hurt most: whoever touches the man.

Not his bed. Not his chair. Him. A hand on the shoulder, an embrace from his wife, a child climbing into his lap — each one carried a cost. Anyone who loved him had to wash and wait till evening.

Touch is how humans say what words cannot. To be untouchable is a particular kind of poverty.

But notice something important: touching him was not forbidden. It carried a consequence, and the consequence was manageable — wash, and wait until evening. God did not command the community to abandon him. He made it costly, and He made it possible.

That is often what love looks like. Not effortless, but willing to pay a small price to stay close. There are people in every church who cost something to love — the demanding one, the grieving one, the one whose life is complicated. Loving them takes time and energy we would rather spend elsewhere.

And then there is Jesus, who reached out his hand and touched the man everyone avoided (Mark 1:41). He did not calculate the cost. He simply touched.

Who needs your touch this week, even if it costs you an evening?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Who in your life costs something to love?
2. Have you avoided someone because caring for them is inconvenient?
3. What would it look like to move towards them this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You touched those everyone else avoided. Give me a willing heart to draw near to people who cost me something, and to love as You loved. Amen.
